headline: GOLD AND SILVER EACH UP 1%+ ON LABOR DAY — Metals Find Footing at $4,398 and $66.75 as Markets Digest September FOMC Risk
snippet: Gold and silver posted gains of more than 1% each in Monday's Labor Day session — a holiday with US markets closed — recovering from last week's Federal Reserve-driven selloff after the August non-farm payrolls beat (162,000 jobs vs. 56,000 consensus) revived September rate-hike bets. Gold traded at $4,398 per ounce and silver at $66.75, with the gold-silver ratio narrowing to 66.7 from Friday's close. SP Angel's Monday morning market view described the move as 'relief from the down week,' noting that precious metals appeared to find technical support at current levels. The September 11 CPI and September 16 FOMC meeting remain the binary catalysts that will define gold's direction for the remainder of Q3.

headline: PALLADIUM SURGES TO $1,408 ON SOUTH AFRICA SUPPLY ALARM — Load-Shedding and Labor Strikes Threaten 90% of Global PGM Supply
snippet: Palladium rose to $1,408.53 per ounce in early September as investors priced in South African supply disruption risk in a market where South Africa, Russia, and Zimbabwe collectively supply approximately 90% of global platinum group metals. South Africa's ongoing power crisis — with load-shedding directly targeting industrial consumers including mines — has combined with fresh labor unrest to raise production shortfall concerns. Platinum held near $1,826 per ounce at multi-month highs. The dynamic offers retail investors a differentiated precious metals exposure: while gold is trading as a macro/policy instrument, PGMs are being driven by supply-side fundamentals independent of interest rate dynamics.

headline: BLOOMBERG: EL NIÑO WATER CRISIS COULD FORCE 40% OUTPUT CUT AT WORLD'S BIGGEST NICKEL HUB — IMIP Warning Sends Philippine Miners Up 14-42%
snippet: Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park, the world's largest nickel processing complex and source of approximately 35% of global refined nickel supply, warned that El Niño-driven water shortages may force output cuts of 30-40% if new water sources are not secured. Hydropower stations supporting IMIP's energy-intensive smelting operations are running severely under capacity due to drought, with the 2026 El Niño event expected to peak in September. The news triggered an immediate market reaction: Philippine nickel miners East Coast Vulcan soared 42%, NiHAO gained 21%, and Nickel Asia climbed 14% as investors priced in a supply shock in a metal approaching its first structural deficit since 2021.

headline: NICKEL HEADS FOR FIRST DEFICIT IN 5 YEARS — Indonesia Supply Shock Plus Iran War 'Rewrite the Supply Map'; Analysts Identify Junior Leverage Plays
snippet: A Peacock Tariff Consulting analysis argues that nickel — which spent 2022 through 2025 mired in structural oversupply from Indonesian HPAL expansion — is approaching its first structural deficit since 2021. Converging supply shocks include El Niño threatening a 40% cut at IMIP, the Iran war's impact on global shipping and energy costs, and Chinese-backed HPAL producers considering coordinated 30% output cuts amid weak prices and rising sulphur costs. The report identifies nickel juniors in stable jurisdictions — Canada, Australia, and Scandinavia — as the highest-leverage play if the deficit thesis confirms, noting that new nickel mines take a decade from discovery to production and the market shifted from surplus to deficit faster than any mine financing cycle can respond.

headline: ANGLO-TECK $53B MEGA-MERGER: 11 TRADING DAYS FROM CLOSING — China and South Korea Approval Are the Last Hurdle; Leadership Team Named
snippet: Teck Resources updated shareholders on September 1 that the transformative $53-billion all-stock merger-of-equals with Anglo American requires only Chinese and South Korean regulatory approval before closing — and that once those approvals are received, the deal closes 11 trading days later. Canadian regulatory clearance was granted in December 2025 and shareholder votes passed with overwhelming support. The combined Anglo Teck entity, whose executive leadership team was announced July 30, will rank among the world's largest diversified miners, with a dominant copper-zinc-steelmaking-coal portfolio. The near-term completion of the largest mining M&A deal in a generation is expected to catalyze further sector consolidation as major miners compete for scale against a structural copper deficit.

headline: DRC COBALT QUOTA CAPS 2026 OUTPUT AT HALF OF 2024 PRODUCTION — 96,600t Annual Limit Creates Structural Supply Pinch; Hydroxide Prices Double YoY
snippet: The Democratic Republic of Congo's cobalt quota system — which replaced the 2025 export ban in October 2025 — caps 2026 production at 96,600 tonnes, less than half of 2024's output of approximately 204,000 tonnes. The structural supply constraint has driven cobalt hydroxide prices to more than double year-over-year, with cobalt sulphate trading above RMB 55,000 per tonne. The DRC quota represents one of the most dramatic supply-side policy interventions in battery materials history, transforming cobalt from a market burdened by sub-$15/lb oversupply in 2024 to a constrained market above $56,000 per tonne in 2026. For junior investors, higher cobalt prices materially improve byproduct credits on many polymetallic nickel and copper projects.

headline: SUREBET SYSTEM GROWS TO 2.01 KM² AS GOLIATH DRILLS 59th OF 98 HOLES — 7 Rigs, 34,990m and $4,400 Gold Power Golden Triangle's Largest Junior Program
snippet: Goliath Resources' (TSXV: GOT) 2026 drilling campaign at the Surebet discovery in British Columbia's Golden Triangle has expanded the system footprint 12% to 2.01 square kilometres, with 59 of 98 planned holes completed and 34,990 metres drilled. The Golden Gate zone expanded 38% to 1.17 km² and the Bonanza zone grew 19% to 1.51 km², with a newly defined volcanic wedge connecting both zones. The 50,000-metre, seven-rig program — the largest single-season junior gold exploration campaign in Canada in 2026 — has returned high-grade intercepts throughout, including 7.38 g/t AuEq over 35.7 metres with visible gold identified in 33 of 52 completed holes. At $4,400 gold, the margin implied for a potential mine at Surebet's grades represents a historic backdrop for pre-resource exploration investors.

headline: GOLD STOCKS AT SEASONAL INFLECTION: DEEPLY OVERSOLD AS AUTUMN RALLY WINDOW OPENS — Historical 10.1% Average Gain; Analysts Flag 30% Miner Upside
snippet: Gold stocks are entering their strongest seasonal juncture — the transition from summer doldrums to autumn rally — at unusually depressed technical levels relative to the gold price, setting up conditions for an amplified rebound. Major gold miners historically leverage material gold moves by 2x to 3x, meaning a 10% autumn gold rally translates to 20-30% miner gains; the historical GDX autumn rally averages 10.1% from late June to late September. Summer 2026 saw anomalous gold selling driven by new-Fed-chair hawkishness fears and geopolitical uncertainty, creating the deeply oversold starting point that historically precedes the largest rallies. The GDX has already broken through prior-high resistance levels that gold itself has not yet cleared — a pattern historically associated with miners leading the metal by approximately one month before broader institutional rotation begins.

headline: LABOR DAY FUTURES: COPPER $14,425, GOLD $4,398, SILVER $66.75 — Broad Metals Rally in Thin Trading Points to Institutional Accumulation at Lows
snippet: With US markets closed for Labor Day, Monday's futures session told a broadly bullish story across the metals complex: copper held at $14,425 per tonne near its all-time LME record of $14,527, gold rose to $4,398, and silver climbed to $66.75. Analysts note that a Labor Day rally in thin markets tends to reflect conviction-based buying rather than algorithmic momentum, since high-frequency traders — the dominant driver of short-term volatility — are largely absent from holiday sessions. The simultaneous strength across gold, silver, and copper suggests institutional accumulation at current levels rather than continuation of last week's technically-driven selling, a meaningful signal for investors trying to assess whether the August-September correction has established a durable floor.

headline: CHINESE EV MAKERS DEMAND 20%+ COBALT DISCOUNTS FROM INDONESIAN HPAL PLANTS — Q4 Deal Season to Spread Supply-Chain Cost Pain Beyond Traders
snippet: Chinese battery manufacturers for electric vehicles are demanding steeper cobalt discounts from Indonesian HPAL producers as fourth-quarter supply contracts come up for renegotiation — a pressure that traders have absorbed to date but is now set to flow through to smelter-level economics. Some HPAL operators are already considering coordinated output cuts of around 30% amid weak cobalt revenues and rising operating costs, though no formal agreement has been reached. The development creates a compounding supply risk: the DRC's 96,600-tonne cobalt quota limits upstream supply while Indonesian HPAL economics deteriorate downstream — a simultaneous squeeze on two of the battery cobalt supply chain's most critical links heading into Q4 2026.
